title: Phase 7 · Information Theory & Compression
outline:
Phase 7 video (Algorithms, ECM3428): 'Information Theory & Compression', sub line 'How files get smaller'. 11 scenes, 120 s: title (4), fixed codes waste bits (10), information is surprise (11), entropy is the average surprise and the floor (12), prefix-free codes (12), Huffman merging (14), reading the codes and encoding (12), LZW encoding (13), LZW decoding (12), GIF payoff (11), recap (9). Story: a fixed code spends the same bits on every letter, so the message BBADEBC costs 21 bits. Information is surprise (halve the chance, add a bit); entropy is the average surprise and no lossless code beats it. A code must be readable without gaps: codewords are the leaves of a tree. Huffman builds the best such tree by merging the two rarest nodes again and again (BBADEBC becomes 15 bits, average 1.98 bits a letter against a floor of 1.96). LZW needs no table: it learns phrases while it reads, and the decoder rebuilds the same dictionary from the codes alone (with the one trick, the entry that arrives early). GIF shows where it pays: runs of one colour shrink, noise does not. Not covered (lessons and workshop): Kraft's inequality (7.4), the cost of a wrong model / KL divergence (7.5), the coin curve H(p) (7.3), Huffman pseudocode, O(n log n) cost and bit-error limits (7.8), lossy compression and rate-distortion (7.12), the lessons' BANANABANDANA demo; the recap points to Workshop 7.W (build the tree).

LESSONS the facts come from: a7-redundancy 7.1 (fixed 3-bit code, BBADEBC, 21 bits), a7-entropy 7.2 (surprise, entropy, the loaded die), a7-binary-entropy 7.3, a7-source-coding 7.4, a7-kl 7.5, a7-huffman 7.6 (prefix-free codes, the greedy merge), a7-huffman-worked 7.7 (the lecture source, codes, 15 bits), a7-huffman-algo 7.8, a7-lzw 7.9 (the shared dictionary), a7-lzw-decode 7.10 (ABABABABA, codes 0 1 2 4 3, the missing entry), a7-gif 7.11 (the pixel row), a7-rate-distortion 7.12, a7-build 7.W (workshop: weather station, build the tree); js/content/algo/algo-p7-*.js, algo-p7-x-*.js, algo-workshops-7-0*.js; bank js/bank/algo-*.js.

THE DATA (all computed and asserted in videos/a7/common.js). SURPRISE: -log2 p for p = 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 bits. ENTROPY: the loaded die A 1/2, B 1/4, C 1/8, D 1/8 has surprises 1, 2, 3, 3 and H = .5 + .5 + .375 + .375 = 1.75 bits; a fixed code needs 2. The 8-symbol sample ABAACABD (A 4, B 2, C 1, D 1 = 8 x the chances) costs 14 surprise-bits against 16 fixed: 14 / 8 = 1.75. LECTURE SOURCE: A .16, B .51, C .09, D .13, E .11 (percent weights 16, 51, 9, 13, 11). Fixed 3-bit code C 000, E 001, D 010, A 011, B 100 (the video numbers the letters rarest first so that B = 1 is legal; the lesson's alphabetical table also gives 21 bits): BBADEBC = 100 100 011 010 001 100 000 = 21 bits. Huffman: merge C .09 + E .11 = CE .20; D .13 + A .16 = DA .29; CE .20 + DA .29 = CEDA .49; CEDA .49 + B .51 = 1.00; the bigger branch is 1 (the lecture's convention): B = 1, A = 011, D = 010, E = 001, C = 000; BBADEBC = 1 1 011 010 001 1 000 = 110110100011000 = 15 bits. Average length L = .51 x 1 + .49 x 3 = 1.98 = .20 + .29 + .49 + 1.00 (the sum of the merge weights); entropy H = 1.964; L - H = 0.016; fixed = 3. PREFIX: bad code A 0, B 1, C 01 (the bits 01 = AB or C); good code A 0, B 10, C 110, D 111 (010110 = A B C). LZW: ABABABABA with A = 0, B = 1: emits 0, 1, 2, 4, 3 and adds AB = 2, BA = 3, ABA = 4, ABAB = 5 (9 letters, 5 codes); the decoder (codes 0 1 2 4 3) outputs A, B (adds AB), AB (adds BA), code 4 unknown -> AB + A = ABA (adds ABA), BA (adds ABAB) = ABABABABA. GIF: AAAAAABBBCCCCCDDDD -> 11 codes (A|AA|AAA|B|BB|C|CC|CC|D|DD|D); the noisy row DBCBAABDADDCDDACCA -> 17 codes.

VIDEO-WIDE CONVENTIONS. COLOURS (whole video): green = the short / compressed / valid result (a short code, the saved bits, a finished tree, a sent or decoded letter, a matched codeword, the Huffman bar); red = waste or ambiguity (bits thrown away, a code with two readings, the noisy row); blue = what we look at now (the current letter or phrase w, the prefix being read, tree branches while they are built, the surprise-source tiles); orange = attention and choices (surprise cells, the two smallest nodes picked, the next letter c, a freshly added dictionary entry, the unknown code and the '?' chip); purple = the rulebook and the limit (the entropy floor and its tags, the dictionary chips); grey = neutral (fixed-code cells and bars, waiting nodes, labels, plain letter tiles). Message letters are plain white tiles (A7.tiles default). One exception, scene 10 only: the four palette colours (A green, B blue, C purple, D orange), always with their letter on the tile. SHARED LAYOUT: figures fill the stage 936 x 640 with at least 12 px margin; the caption sits under the stage and never overlaps it; text is 28 px or more everywhere (A7 helpers refuse smaller); tiles and strips are aligned to the 12 px grid used in the specs; the code tree puts the root on top and leaves at the bottom. REUSE OF DATA: scene 2, 6, 7 share the lecture source and the message BBADEBC (21 bits in scene 2 -> 15 bits in scene 7; B = 1 is the same shortening in both); scene 3 and 4 share the chances 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 (the legend of scene 4 repeats the ladder of scene 3); scene 5 uses its own small code to show prefix-freeness and decoding; scenes 8 and 9 share ABABABABA and the codes 0 1 2 4 3 (9 learns the same dictionary 8 built); scene 10 uses the lesson's pixel row. WORDS defined on screen before use: 'bit' (one yes-or-no answer, scene 3), 'entropy' (scene 4 title + counter), 'floor' (scene 4 tag, reused in scene 6), 'prefix-free' (a tag in scene 5 after the picture), 'dictionary' (a purple tag in scene 8). Symbols (ticks, crosses, plus, equals) are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / A7.sym), never glyphs. Every scene's numbers come from the logs in videos/a7/common.js (A7.REDUNDANCY, LADDER, DIE, SAMPLE, BAD, PREFIX, HUFF, ENCODE, LZW, LZW_DEC, GIF), which assert every value when the page loads and throw a clear Error if one differs from this storyboard. The title card (scene-01-title.js) is finished (a copy of VID.titleCard with a two-line 80 px headline, because 'Information Theory & Compression' does not fit one line) and must not be replaced.

title: Every letter costs
the same bits
caps: A fixed code spends 3 bits on every letter.
That is 21 bits for BBADEBC.
But B turns up three times.
Common letters get short codes: 15 bits.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: a fixed-length code gives every letter the same 3 bits, so the message BBADEBC (7 letters) costs 21 bits although B is three of the seven. Give B a one-bit code, keep the others, and the total drops to 15. The viewer meets the question the rest of the video answers: how short can the codes get, and how do we build them?

title: Rare news carries
more information
caps: News we expect tells us nothing: 0 bits.
Half the chance: one yes-or-no answer, 1 bit.
Each time the chance halves, one more bit.
Rarer news tells us more.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: information is surprise, measured in bits. A ladder of five rows: the chance of the news halves from row to row (certain, 1 in 2, 1 in 4, 1 in 8, 1 in 16) and each halving adds exactly one bit (0, 1, 2, 3, 4). A bit is one yes-or-no answer. Rare news carries more information.

title: Average surprise
is the entropy
caps: A source sends four symbols with these chances.
Here are eight symbols it sent.
Each one costs its surprise in bits.
Fixed: 16 bits. Surprise: only 14.
1.75 bits a symbol is the floor.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: entropy is the AVERAGE surprise, and it is the floor for compression. A source sends A, B, C or D with chances 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8 (surprise 1, 2, 3, 3 bits from scene 3). A sample of eight symbols that has exactly those chances (ABAACABD: A four times, B twice, C and D once) costs 1+2+1+1+3+1+2+3 = 14 bits of surprise; a fixed 2-bit code needs 16. 14 / 8 = 1.75 bits a symbol is the entropy: no lossless code averages less.
COLOURS (whole video): green = the short / compressed / valid result (a short code, the saved bits, a finished tree, a decoded letter, a matched codeword); red = waste or ambiguity (bits we throw away, a code with two readings, the noisy row); blue = what we are looking at now (the current letter, the phrase w, a prefix being read, tree branches while they are built); orange = attention and choices (surprise cells, the two smallest nodes picked, the next letter c, a new dictionary entry, the unknown code); purple = the rulebook and the limit (the entropy floor, the dictionary chips); grey = neutral (fixed-code cells, waiting nodes, baseline bars). title: Codes you can read
without any gaps
caps: Codes sit side by side, with no gaps.
01 could be A then B…
…or C. Two readings!
Put every code at a branch end.
Follow the bits down. A leaf means a letter is done.
No code starts another.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: without gaps between codewords the decoder must know where one ends. A code is only readable if no codeword starts another. Part 1 shows a bad code (A=0, B=1, C=01: the bits 01 read as A then B, or as C). Part 2 puts the good code A=0, B=10, C=110, D=111 on a tree: every codeword is a LEAF, so a walk from the root that reaches a leaf has finished a letter, and the stream 010110 reads A B C in only one way.
COLOURS (whole video): green = the short / compressed / valid result (a short code, the saved bits, a finished tree, a decoded letter, a matched codeword); red = waste or ambiguity (bits we throw away, a code with two readings, the noisy row); blue = what we are looking at now (the current letter, the phrase w, a prefix being read, tree branches while they are built); orange = attention and choices (surprise cells, the two smallest nodes picked, the next letter c, a new dictionary entry, the unknown code); purple = the rulebook and the limit (the entropy floor, the dictionary chips); grey = neutral (fixed-code cells, waiting nodes, baseline bars). Here: blue = the bits / path being read, green = a finished letter and the prefix-free verdict, red = the two readings of the bad code.

PART 1 (0.3-5.6; everything in it fades out 5.2-5.6 with o = 1 - ramp(t, 5.2, 5.6)). book1 = A7.tiles(stage, {x: 316, y: 24, items: [{text: 'A', sub: '0'}, {text: 'B', sub: '1'}, {text: 'C', sub: '01'}], w: 88, h: 104, gap: 20, fs: 44}); rec = A7.tag(stage, {x: 180, y: 222, text: 'received', tone: 'grey'}); bitsRow = A7.bits(stage, {x: 400, y: 204, groups: '01', cell: 72, h: 72, gap: 8, fs: 44, tone: 'blue'}) (two cells, x 400-552); reading 1: A7.tiles(stage, {x: 400, y: 320, items: ['A', 'B'], w: 72, h: 80, gap: 8, fs: 44}) with tone blue (each tile under its bit cell) plus a grey tag 'reading 1' at (180, 336); reading 2: A7.tiles(stage, {x: 400, y: 440, items: ['C'], w: 152, h: 80, fs: 44}) (one tile spanning both cells) plus a grey tag 'reading 2' at (180, 456); verdict: A7.tag(stage, {x: 620, y: 388, text: 'two readings!', tone: 'red', solid: true}) and a red L5.cross(580, 420, 70, 'red', {w: 12}) from L5.svg(stage) drawn on beside it. PART 2 (5.7-12). P = A7.PREFIX; pos = A7.treePos(P.tree, {x0: 150, slot: 130, top: 30, dy: 130}); T = A7.tree(stage, {tree: P.tree, pos, leafH: 80}). Node centres: root (329, 30), leaf A (215, 160), inner '1' (443, 160), leaf B (345, 290), inner '11' (540, 290), leaf C (475, 420), leaf D (605, 420); leaf tiles show the letter and its codeword (A 0, B 10, C 110, D 111); inner nodes are small dots. stream = A7.bits(stage, {x: 40, y: 520, groups: P.stream, cell: 56, h: 56, gap: 6, fs: 36, tone: 'grey'}) (six cells '010110', x 40-412); out = A7.tiles(stage, {x: 520, y: 516, items: [...P.out], w: 72, h: 64, gap: 12, fs: 40}) (the decoded letters A B C appear one by one, tone green); tok = A7.token(stage, {tone: 'blue'}); verdict = A7.tag(stage, {x: 690, y: 190, text: 'prefix-free', tone: 'green', solid: true}).
Timeline: 5.7-6.8 the tree builds top-down: nodes pop 0.12 s apart (T.update nodes k), each branch grows (edge k) and its 0 / 1 sticker pops (edge bit) 0.1 s later; 6.9-7.4 the stream cells pop; the token pops on the root at 7.3. WALK: bit i (P.walk[i] = {i, bit, from, to, leaf, out, start, end}) starts at 7.5 + 0.5 i and takes 0.4 s: the token goes from T.pt(from) to T.pt(to) (E.inOut) but STOPS AT THE TOP EDGE of a leaf (y - T.size(id).h / 2) so the letter stays readable; stream cell i turns blue (cells patch tone 'blue') while it belongs to the current codeword (cells start..i). When the walk reaches a leaf (walk[i].leaf): the leaf turns solid green (nodes patch solid true, tone 'green') with a ring pulse, the codeword's cells turn green, the letter pops into out (tile index out.length - 1), and the token hops back to the root (fade out 0.15 s, pop at the root 0.15 s) before the next bit. Arrival times: A 7.9, B 8.9, C 10.4. 10.5 the green 'prefix-free' tag pops.

IDEA: Huffman coding. Keep a pool of nodes, each with a chance. Merge the two SMALLEST into a new node whose chance is their sum, put it back, repeat until one node (the root) is left. title: LZW learns phrases
as it reads
caps: LZW starts with a tiny dictionary: A and B.
A new longer phrase: send a code, learn it.
Known? Keep growing.
Still known: grow again.
Longer phrases get one code each.
Nine letters became five codes.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: LZW (Lempel-Ziv-Welch) learns repeated phrases while it reads. The lecture's example: message ABABABABA, alphabet A = 0, B = 1. Keep a phrase w (blue) and look at the next letter c (orange). If w + c is already in the dictionary, w just grows. If it is new: send the code of w, add w + c to the dictionary, and start again from c. Result: codes 0 1 2 4 3, nine letters become five codes, and the dictionary grew to AB = 2, BA = 3, ABA = 4, ABAB = 5.

Here: blue = the phrase w, orange = the next letter c and a freshly added entry, green = letters already sent and the codes sent, purple = the dictionary.

title: The decoder rebuilds

title: Repeats shrink,
noise does not
caps: A GIF packs its pixels with LZW.
Runs of one colour shrink into single codes.
Noise rarely repeats, so almost nothing shrinks.
LZW feeds on repeats.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: the real-world payoff. A GIF stores each pixel as a palette colour (a letter here) and packs the rows with LZW. Runs of one colour are repeats, so they shrink; noise has almost no repeats, so almost nothing shrinks. The lesson row AAAAAABBBCCCCCDDDD (6 A, 3 B, 5 C, 4 D) parses into 11 pieces (A | AA | AAA | B | BB | C | CC | CC | D | DD | D) = 11 codes for 18 pixels; a noisy row DBCBAABDADDCDDACCA of the same 18 pixels needs 17 codes (my own example: the lesson only says noise saves little).
COLOURS (whole video): green = the short / compressed / valid result (a short code, the saved bits, a finished tree, a decoded letter, a matched codeword); red = waste or ambiguity (bits we throw away, a code with two readings, the noisy row); blue = what we are looking at now (the current letter, the phrase w, a prefix being read, tree branches while they are built); orange = attention and choices (surprise cells, the two smallest nodes picked, the next letter c, a new dictionary entry, the unknown code); purple = the rulebook and the limit (the entropy floor, the dictionary chips); grey = neutral (fixed-code cells, waiting nodes, baseline bars). Here the four palette colours are the only exception: tiles A green, B blue, C purple, D orange (solid, with their letter in the -on shade, A7.GIF.tones), always labelled with the letter so no meaning is carried by colour alone. The parse spans are blue, the verdict tags green (flat) and red (noisy).

LAYOUT (stage px; G = A7.GIF). Two rows: flat (y 24) and noisy (y 300). For each row (text = G.flat.text / G.noisy.text, chunks = G.flat.chunks / G.noisy.chunks): label = A7.tag(stage, {x: 20, y, text: 'a GIF row: flat colour' | 'a GIF row: noisy', tone: 'grey'}); px = A7.tiles(stage, {x: 20, y: y + 58, items: [...text].map((c) => ({text: c, tone: G.tones[c]})), w: 46, h: 46, gap: 4, fs: 28}) with solid true on every tile (18 tiles, x 20-916; tile j spans x 20 + 50 j .. +46); one A7.span(stage, {x: 20 + 50 c.from, y: y + 120, w: 50 (c.to - c.from) - 4, h: 14, tone: 'blue'}) per chunk (flat 11, noisy 17); count = A7.tag(stage, {x: 20, y: y + 148, text: '18 pixels, 0 codes', tone: 'grey'}). Rows: flat label y 24, tiles y 82, spans y 144, count y 172; noisy label y 300, tiles y 358, spans y 420, count y 448. Footer: A7.tag(stage, {x: 20, y: 548, text: 'GIF stores its pixels this way', tone: 'purple'}).

DATA (asserted): G.flat.count 11 (chunks A|AA|AAA|B|BB|C|CC|CC|D|DD|D; with palette numbers from 1 the codes are 1,5,6,2,8,3,10,10,4,13,4 as in lesson 7.11; do not print code numbers), G.noisy.count 17 (chunks: 16 single pixels and one DD). Show only the COUNT of codes.

TIMELINE (local s). 0.2-0.5 the flat label pops; 0.3-1.3 its 18 tiles pop (0.04 s apart, solid); 1.3 the count tag pops ('18 pixels, 0 codes'). PARSE flat: chunk c appears at 1.5 + 0.27 c (11 chunks, last at 4.2): its span grows over its tiles (k 0.2 s) and the count text becomes `18 pixels, ${c + 1} codes`; 4.6-4.9 the count tag turns solid green. Noisy row: label and tiles pop 5.0-6.0, count tag 6.0; PARSE noisy: chunk c at 6.1 + 0.12 c (17 chunks, last at 8.0), count counts up the same way; 8.2-8.5 the count tag turns solid red. 8.8-9.2 the footer tag pops. Hold still to 11.
Pitfalls: both rows must stay inside x 20-916; labels are 28 px; use the tone of a tag for emphasis, never opacity below 1; the spans of neighbouring chunks are separated by a 4 px gap so the pieces read as separate.

CAPTION SYNC: [0.4-2.6] the label 'a GIF row' and the pixel tiles; [3.4-5.2] the flat parse (1.5-4.5) and its green count (4.6); [5.8-8.2] the noisy parse (6.1-8.0); [8.4-10.4] the red count (8.2) and the footer.
END STATE: two rows, 11 blue spans under the flat row (green '18 pixels, 11 codes'), 17 spans under the noisy row (red '18 pixels, 17 codes'), purple footer tag.

helpers:
FILES: videos/a7/common.js (data and algorithms, pure, no DOM, 364 code lines), videos/a7/common-2.js (A7.tag, tiles, chips, bits, counter, bar, span, token, sym), videos/a7/common-3.js (A7.treePos, A7.tree). Everything hangs off window.VID.a7; scenes start with const V = window.VID, A7 = V.a7, L5 = V.l5 and const {ramp, flash, lerp, ease: E} = V. videos/algo-7.html loads engine.js, cards.js, l5/common.js, then a7/common.js, common-2.js, common-3.js, then scene-01 ... scene-11, audio/algo-7.js. l6 is not loaded. EVERY helper file starts with a long API comment listing every signature, option and return value: READ THEM FIRST, they are the contract (they were tested with throw-away prototypes of scenes 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, see the coordinates in the specs). All draw calls are PURE: create each piece once in build(stage), call its set / update every frame from update(t) with everything you want to see; nothing is remembered between frames; no Math.random, Date or timers (A7.rng(seed) is seeded). Never dim text below opacity 1 once it is on screen: switch the TONE (grey) instead, or fade the whole group out.

A. DATA (common.js): A7.LETTERS, PCT, MSG, ORDER, FIXED, REDUNDANCY {fixed, short, fixedTotal 21, shortTotal 15, saved 6, counts}; LADDER (p, frac, say, bits); DIE {letters, p, frac, bits, share, H 1.75}; SAMPLE {msg, bits, total 14, fixedTotal 16, perSymbol 1.75}; BAD {codes, stream, readings}; PREFIX {codes, stream, out, tree, walk}; codeTree(codes); HUFF {nodes, merges, roots, smallest, edges, codes, order, L 1.98, H 1.964, costs}; huffman(items); ENCODE {codes, bits, count 15, fixed, fixedBits, fixedCount 21, saved 6}; LZW {text, alpha, steps, codes, chunks, dict, entries}; LZW_DEC {steps, out}; lzwEncode / lzwDecode; GIF {alpha, tones, flat, noisy}; ek(parent, child); fmtW(percent) -> '.20'; fmtBits(percent) -> '1.98'; entropy(ps); surprise(p); rng, same, close, sum, mix, cyc, TONES.

B. SMALL PIECES (common-2.js): A7.tag(parent, {x, y, text, tone, solid, fs, h}) -> t.set({text, tone, solid, k, x, y, s, o}); A7.tiles(parent, {x, y, items, w, h, gap, dir, fs, subFs}) -> row.set(i, {text, sub, tone, solid, ghost, plain, ring, ringK, k, x, y, s, o}), row.all(fn), row.pos(i), row.mid(i) (a tile with no tone is a plain white tile); A7.chips(parent, {x, y, items: [{idx, text}], cols, w 180, h 60, ...}) -> board.set(i, {...}) the same way (dictionary entries 'idx | text'); A7.bits(parent, {x, y, groups, cell, h, gap, groupGap, fs, digits, tone}) -> b.set({k, groupK, tone, tones, solid, cells: {i: patch}, o, x, y, s}), b.cell(i), b.group(g), b.width (a bit strip, one group per codeword; per-cell patches carry offsets for flying or falling cells); A7.counter(parent, {x, y, w, h, label, tone}) -> c.set({text, tone, solid, bump, k, o}); A7.bar(parent, {x, y, w, h, tone, solid, text, fs}) -> b.set({k, tone, solid, text, textOut, o}), b.end(k); A7.span(parent, {x, y, w, h, tone}) -> s.set({x, w, k, tone, dash, o}) (a rounded line under tiles); A7.token(parent, {tone, size}) -> m.set({x, y, s, o, tone}) (centre coordinates); A7.sym(kind, x, y, size, tone) -> SVG <g> for 'plus' | 'minus' | 'equals'. Tones: grey, green, red, orange, blue, purple. k 0..1 pops a piece in (0 = hidden); x, y in set() are offsets from the piece's slot.

C. THE TREE (common-3.js): A7.treePos(tree, {x0, slot, top, dy, flat}) -> {id: [x, y]} node centres (tree = A7.HUFF or a tree from A7.codeTree; flat 0..1 slides leaves from their own depth to the bottom row); T = A7.tree(parent, {tree, pos, r, leafW, leafH, ew, label}); T.update({nodes: {id: tone | {tone, solid, k, o, s, dx, dy, ring, ringK, ringDash, text, sub}}, edges: {'p>c': tone | {tone, k, o, w, bit, bitTone, bitSolid, dash}}, pos: {id: [x, y]} (moving nodes, branches follow), base: {node, edge} (state of unlisted ones; default hidden), o}); T.pt(id), T.mid(p, c, f), T.size(id), T.ids, T.keys. Default labels: A7.HUFF leaf = letter + weight, inner = weight; a code tree leaf = letter + codeword, inner = a dot. Tested positions are in the specs of scenes 5, 6 and 7 (keep top >= 52 for r 38 circles; dy >= 140 with leafH 92).

D. L5 (l5/common.js) pictograms: L5.tick(x, y, size, tone, {w, on, ink}), L5.cross(...), L5.arrow(x1, y1, x2, y2, tone, o, {w, head, bow}), L5.drawOn(g, k) (draw-on 0..1), L5.svg(parent, w, h) (a full-stage SVG to append pictograms to), L5.tone(name) (CSS var strings for your own SVG).
